text: Kit Fine ('Essence and Modality', 1994) argues that essence is correctly defined as de re necessity: x is essentially F just in case necessarily, if x exists then Fx.
explanation: False. Fine argues the reverse — the modal account is extensionally wrong. Socrates is necessarily a member of {Socrates}, so the modal definition would make that membership part of his essence, which it is not. Essence is finer-grained (hyperintensional) than necessity, and modal facts should instead be grounded in essences.
